title: Autotune: defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and caching, introduced quantization profile presets, and new unit-economics CLI and dashboard integration. No breaking changes expected.
description: Context: Customers run a wide variety of workloads; unit token cost is highly sensitive to batching, prefix caching, and quantization choices. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce per-token cost without degrading latency SLOs; 2) a set of vetted quantization profile presets (int8/int4 variants) and runtime selection logic; 3) unit-economics tooling to estimate per-request cost and recommend safe rollouts. Motivation: reduce operator configuration burden, cut average hosted token cost ~15-25% for common RL/assistant workloads, and provide visibility for customers and SREs. This description is a single continuous string with sections below. Checklist: - [x] Add autotune config and default profiles - [x] Implement quantization profile selection runtime hook - [x] Add unit-econ CLI that samples live traces and computes per-token cost - [x] Integrate unit-econ results into Console cost dashboard - [x] Add e2e tests and perf canary - [x] Docs + migration notes Changes in this PR: - Autotune: new subsystem under /server/autotune that analyzes request size distribution and adjusts batching windows and prefix-KV caching TTLs. Default policy is conservative for latency-bound routes and aggressive for throughput-bound routes. - Quant profiles: presets under /models/quant_profiles.json and selection logic in runtime compiler that prefers lower-precision variants when eval QA and perf regression bounds are met. - Unit-econ tooling: CLI at tools/uecon/ that ingests traces, applies cost model (GPU token cost + infra overhead), and emits recommendations. Also a small Console plugin to show projected cost delta for rollout. Migration notes: existing configs are honored by default; new autotune is opt-in per-route via: route.config.autotune.enabled = true. We ship a rollout that enables autotune for low-traffic customers first, then progressively to higher tiers after 72h canary. Why not fully automatic by default: we keep explicit opt-in to avoid workload surprises; recommendations are surfaced before any auto-change in account scope. Performance: see perf_results. Rollout plan: staged via feature flag feature.autotune.why:enable -> canary group (5%) -> 25% -> 100% if metrics OK. Backout path: feature flag off + revert quant profile selection (config toggle) will restore previous behavior. Related: ENG-4321, PM-1187.
